beats.b01: Hi, I'm Orbit, AIA's knowledge copilot. Here's what I do, in two minutes.
beats.b02: The rules that run our business live in old COBOL programs. Only a few specialists can read them, so a hard question takes seven to fifteen days, and the knowledge walks out when they leave.
beats.b03: Ask me in plain English. Choose a business view or a technical view, watch the answer stream in live, and I'll suggest what to ask next.
beats.b04: I make the rules visible: business rules, decision tables, process flows and a data dictionary, all built from the code itself.
beats.b05: Put a real scenario to me. I trace it step by step through the programs and show the outcome, in minutes, not days.
beats.b06: Every answer cites the programs behind it, and you can open the code. Guards block prompt injection and personal-data requests.
beats.b07: Before anything changes, I show what it would touch: directly, also, and downstream, in an impact map and a report.
beats.b08: Then I draft the functional requirement and the test scenarios, from how the system really behaves, ready to export.
beats.b09: My coding agent goes further. It finds the place, writes the change, checks it with a real COBOL compiler, and a person reviews the difference.
beats.b10: It's built to run as a service: sign-in, history, admin insights on quality and usage, and security monitoring.
beats.b11: For business owners, answers on demand. For specialists, fewer repeat questions. For AIA, faster change, lower risk and a stronger audit trail.
beats.b12: The timing is right. Seventy percent of business transactions are said to run on COBOL, and MAS is proposing tighter change controls. A hundred routine questions a month is about two hundred hours back, an illustration.
beats.b13: Let's prove it together. Just ask Orbit.
